Hi Alicia — Ben here (Finance Ops). I reviewed your questionnaire and PO template. Below are the practical PO requirements and the routing options depending on how you want to transact:

Option A — Marketplace listing (preferred if you want consolidated billing):
- You list through AWS/Azure/GCP as a seller and customers buy via the marketplace. Marketplace handles invoicing; Redwood receives settlement from the marketplace.
- For our records we need: marketplace seller-id, SKU list (or pricing tiers), and expected monthly committed spend (if any).
- Please provide a marketplace-specific PO or reference if Zephyr issues one to Redwood for internal tracking.

Option B — Direct PO to Redwood (used for private deals / reserved capacity):
- PO must include: Redwood Inference, Inc. (legal name), Redwood remit address, Redwood tax ID: 94-1234567, invoice frequency (monthly or on acceptance), and billing contact.
- Send PO to procure@redwood.com. Our AP team processes net30 by default; if you need different terms, note that in the PO and we will escalate.

Minimum PO fields we require for direct POs:
- PO number
- Billing entity name + remit address
- Billing contact email
- Line item description, unit price, quantity, and total
- Tax ID and country of registration

I attached a short step sheet that outlines the internal workflow (who approves, where to send, timeline). If you're going marketplace-first, Laura — can you confirm the upload checklist (certifications, logos, CSA, 1-pager)?

Attachments: [Attachment: Redwood_PO_Process_Steps.pdf (pdf)]

If Zephyr prefers to keep billing through the marketplace, we can avoid a separate direct PO. If you'd rather we accept a direct PO for initial commitment, send it to procure@redwood.com and we'll expedite.

Ben Carter
Finance Operations Lead
Redwood Inference
